intro.body: Pharmacy First is an NHS community pharmacy service for some common minor illnesses. Contact the pharmacy to confirm how Pharmacy First is currently arranged. The pharmacy team will ask appropriate questions. Suitability and next steps are determined individually.

Pharmacy First sits in community pharmacy and is intended for some common minor illnesses. It does not replace GP, NHS 111 or emergency care. Contact the pharmacy to confirm how the service is currently arranged.

If you are considering Pharmacy First from your area, start by contacting the pharmacy. The team will ask appropriate questions about your symptoms and medicines. Suitability and next steps are determined individually.

Pharmacy First is a structured pharmacy service for some common minor illnesses. Where the service is not appropriate, you will be advised where to seek further help. Contact the pharmacy to confirm how it is currently arranged.
People travelling from your area can contact the pharmacy about Pharmacy First. The pharmacy team will ask appropriate questions. Suitability is not assumed from your postcode.

trustSafety.heading: When To Contact A GP, NHS 111 Or Emergency Services
trustSafety.body: Contact your GP, NHS 111, or urgent care if symptoms keep worsening or suggest a more serious infection. Seek urgent medical care for breathing difficulties, chest pain, severe dehydration, confusion, a non-blanching rash, or any emergency symptoms. If you are unsure after symptoms start in your area, contact the pharmacy to ask whether Pharmacy First is the right enquiry.
bullets: Use GP, NHS 111 or urgent care

trustSafety.heading: When To Contact A GP, NHS 111 Or Emergency Services
trustSafety.body: Pharmacy First is not the right service for every illness in your area. Return to your GP, NHS 111 or urgent care when symptoms persist, worsen, or suggest a more serious infection. Pregnancy, very young children, or problems already under GP review usually need medical assessment instead.

trustSafety.heading: When To Contact A GP, NHS 111 Or Emergency Services
trustSafety.body: Choose GP, NHS 111 or urgent care when symptoms are escalating, unusually severe, or clearly outside Pharmacy First. Seek urgent medical care for breathing difficulties, chest pain, severe dehydration, confusion, a non-blanching rash, or any emergency symptoms. Contact the pharmacy if suitability is unclear before you travel from your area.
bullets: Advice on where to seek help

trustSafety.heading: When To Contact A GP, NHS 111 Or Emergency Services
trustSafety.body: Do not travel from your area if symptoms already look more serious than a community pharmacy conversation. Seek urgent medical care for breathing difficulties, chest pain, severe dehydration, confusion, a non-blanching rash, or any emergency symptoms. Where Pharmacy First is not appropriate, you will be advised where to seek further help.

mythVsFact.heading: Common Misconceptions
mythVsFact.body: Pharmacy First supports some common minor illnesses. It does not replace urgent care for serious illness.
bullets: Myth: Every illness can be managed under Pharmacy First. Fact: Only some common minor illnesses may be considered.
Myth: Pharmacy care replaces emergency services. Fact: Severe or emergency symptoms need urgent medical care.
Myth: Suitability is assumed from your location. Fact: The pharmacy team confirms suitability during the conversation.

faqs.question: What is Pharmacy First?
faqs.answer: It is an NHS service delivered in community pharmacy for some common minor illnesses. The team can explain how it is currently run when you get in touch.

faqs.question: How do I arrange Pharmacy First?
faqs.answer: Get in touch with the pharmacy. Staff will explain the current arrangement and ask the questions they need.

faqs.question: What happens when I contact the pharmacy?
faqs.answer: Expect a conversation about your symptoms and the medicines you take. What happens next depends on your own circumstances.

faqs.question: What if Pharmacy First is not appropriate for my symptoms?
faqs.answer: The team will tell you who to speak to next. That may include your GP, NHS 111 or urgent care if that is safer.

faqs.question: What should I have ready when I get in touch?
faqs.answer: A list of your medicines, when symptoms began, and any allergies. Mention pregnancy or breastfeeding if they apply.

faqs.question: Can children use Pharmacy First?
faqs.answer: Age limits can apply. Ask the pharmacy team whether this service may be suitable for a child.

faqs.question: Does Pharmacy First replace my GP?
faqs.answer: No. It sits alongside GP care for some common minor illnesses. Ongoing and complex conditions stay with your GP.

faqs.question: Is the conversation confidential?
faqs.answer: Yes, pharmacy advice is confidential. Ask how a private conversation is currently set up.

faqs.question: Should I contact the pharmacy before travelling from your area?
faqs.answer: That is a good idea, so you can hear how the service is currently run before you change your plans.

faqs.question: What if I am already seeing my GP for the same problem?
faqs.answer: Mention this when you get in touch. Issues already under GP review often need medical assessment instead.

faqs.question: Can I use Pharmacy First for any illness?
faqs.answer: No. Only some common minor illnesses may be considered. The team will confirm whether it may be suitable for you.

faqs.question: What should I do if symptoms get worse?
faqs.answer: If symptoms worsen, persist, or include emergency warning signs, use your GP, NHS 111 or urgent care. Do not wait for a pharmacy conversation.
